name: Matryoshka image (recursive nesting)

pipeline: encrypt payload with a per-level key
encode into level-N carrier via image-lsb
the level-N stego becomes the payload for level-(N-1)
technical_body.detection: chi-square + RS fire on the outermost carrier; each successive extraction produces another PNG until the innermost flag emerges
technical_body.solution_arc: stegg_lsb_smart_scan → save output → stegg_lsb_smart_scan on the output → repeat until non-image emerges

notes: Compound technique. Each level is an image-lsb hide whose payload happens to be a valid PNG containing another hide. The classic CTF Russian-doll pattern.

name: Chained carriers (image → zip → audio → spectrogram)

pipeline: outer PNG with trailing ZIP after IEND
WAV's spectrogram reveals the flag as text
technical_body.detection: binwalk on the outer image finds the ZIP; extract the WAV; open in Audacity/Sonic Visualiser with the spectrogram view
technical_body.solution_arc: stegg_detect_trailing → stegg_carve → unzip → open WAV in a spectral tool

notes: Format-diverse chain: each stage is a valid file of a different type. Common at DEF CON steg puzzles.

name: Polyglot triggers prompt injection

pipeline: craft a file valid as two formats
one format-parser reads a benign payload
the other extracts a prompt-injection or hidden-instruction payload (often via Unicode tag chars or image ALT text)
technical_body.detection: run the file through both interpreters and diff the parsed content; look for Unicode tag characters in extracted text or ALT
technical_body.solution_arc: identify both formats (`file`, `binwalk`), extract with each parser, compare

notes: The 2024-era AI-agent-attack lineage. Combines Ange Albertini's polyglot canon with the Unicode tag block prompt injection wave.

name: Spectrogram-hidden image

pipeline: render source text/image as a spectrogram-shaped waveform
technical_body.detection: open in Audacity → Spectrogram view, or Sonic Visualiser with an FFT window
technical_body.solution_arc: any audio file in a steg CTF → spectrogram view is the second thing to try after LSB
technical_body.worked_example: Aphex Twin's track 'ΔMi−1 = −α ∑n=1N Di[n]' (formula-titled, sometimes indexed as 'Equation' or track 2) on the 1999 Windowlicker EP contains a rendered image of Richard D. James's face in its final ~30 seconds, visible when the audio is opened in a spectrogram view.
technical_body.provenance: The name of the track is literally the equation for delta modulation. The spectrogram-face is documented in Aphex Twin fan forums since ~1999 and picked up by mainstream press (BBC 2015 retrospective, various music-technology writeups). Not folklore — anyone with sox or Audacity can reproduce the view directly from the released audio.

notes: The single audio-steg trick that always shows up in DEF CON badges. Cheap for the author, high-impact for the solver.

name: Unicode tag block jailbreak / prompt injection

pipeline: append a U+E0020..U+E007E ASCII-shadow payload with prompt-injection instructions
target LLM tokenizer preserves the tag chars and the model reads them as instructions
technical_body.detection: raw byte inspection; the payload is one tag codepoint per printable-ASCII character of the hidden instruction
technical_body.solution_arc: hex-dump the suspect text → look for U+E0000..U+E007F range → decode via ASCII-shadow (subtract 0xE0000, cast to byte)

notes: The 2024 hidden-prompt-injection wave. Ties directly to text-invisible-ink; the ST3GG jailbreak_core composers stitch this with obfuscation transforms.

name: Alpha-channel-only hide

pipeline: set RGB to any innocent content
technical_body.detection: chi-square screams on alpha but is quiet on RGB; visual attack on alpha bit-plane exposes the payload
technical_body.solution_arc: stegg_triage → notice alpha-only anomaly → stegg_decode_manual channels='A' bits_per_channel=1

notes: Frequently mis-diagnosed as 'encrypted RGB' (see myth-lsb-alpha-payload). Alpha all-ones means fully-opaque source, not payload.

name: PNG private-chunk metadata hide

pipeline: add a 4-char private chunk (lowercase second char = private, uppercase first char = ancillary) containing the payload
technical_body.detection: stegg_read_png_chunks lists every chunk; the odd 4-char type is the tell
technical_body.solution_arc: stegg_read_metadata → notice unfamiliar chunk name → stegg_read_png_chunks → extract the chunk data

notes: Survives Slack upload where the named text chunks don't (per sv-png-private-chunk-slack-upload). Common author-friendly hide with a cheap solver arc.
